question: How do light-dependent reactions provide the energy carriers used by the Calvin cycle?
answer_text: The light-dependent reactions convert light energy into chemical energy [ev_008] by using photosystems and electron transport chains to produce the energy carriers ATP and NADPH [ev_002] [ev_010]. These energy carriers are considered "full" because they transport this stored energy from the light-dependent reactions into the stroma where the Calvin cycle reactions take place [ev_001] [ev_005] [ev_007]. Once the energy is released for the Calvin cycle, the "empty" energy carriers return to the light-dependent reactions to obtain more energy [ev_001] [ev_005].
core_reply_assessment: The reply names ATP and NADPH, describes their production through light-driven photosystems/electron transport and transfer to Calvin-cycle reactions, and describes return of spent carriers. This records what the answer says; support of every claim is not independently established by the single retained source body.
